svg.text: A3 TURRET PRESS — dies index, one ram strikes, food falls
Tubes on an upper turret, dies in a die turret, vessels on a carousel: any tube over any die over any vessel, by rotation only.
10 axes (+3 for an optional pick arm)
one fixed ram 3 kN, 300 mm stroke
dice 8 s per piece · patty 4 s, ± 1–2 % mass
SECTION along the turret ring (unrolled: turning = sliding sideways)
TOP VIEW: three turrets on one column, indexed by rotation
orange mark = the ram: whatever is under it gets pushed
Every cut and every shape = push through a die
The die plate is a flat disc with through holes and no blind cavities; it turns
through a fixed wash sector (jets above and below). Tubes are open cylinders whose
floor is the die plate; tubes, pistons and vessels go to the wash chamber.
Weak spot: eggs, slices, breading (pick, place, spread) need an extra arm.
1/8 The brush rollers singulate the potatoes; one drops end-on into the 60 × 60 tube waiting at LOAD.
2/8 Index: the upper turret brings the tube to the ram; the grid die and an empty vessel are already below it.
3/8 The ram pushes the potato through the 10 mm grid; the cut-off blade swings every 10 mm → cubes fall into the vessel.
4/8 Index: the mince tube over the mould cavity; the carousel turns 45° so the pan waits under the knock-out punch.
5/8 The ram fills the mould (0.5 bar); the die turret turns 45°, shearing the patty flat; the punch drops it into the pan.
6/8 Index: the tube of boiled potatoes over the 3 mm ricer die, the pot below.
7/8 The follower piston presses: mash falls into the pot, the skins stay in the tube.
8/8 Wash: the die plate turns through the fixed wash sector — every die is sprayed from above and below.
